title: The page says what is using the disk, how fast the transcript archive grows, and how long the disk lasts at that rate
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`fleet`: the health's `disk` and `memory`, read at the request), crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs (`report`, `free_bytes`), crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (`fleet_health`), the transcript archive's layout (crates/spawn-core transcripts: `<root>/.transcripts/<agent>/<native>[.<n>].jsonl`, and `<root>/.transcripts-progress`), web/src/fleet.ts (`FleetHealth`, `disk`), web/src/resources.ts, Home's host section ("Every agent and the host · health · resources", web/src/components/home), and docs/storage.md.

The problem: storage is one of the owner's two core tracks (sync/roadmap-effects.md, "Core tracks: storage": "the owner can see on the page what is using the disk and how long it lasts"). The owner's order of 2026-11-12 01:00 makes one of 064-066 a storage objective about showing growth: transcripts are never deleted, by the owner's ruling, so their growth is the figure to watch.
- The transcript archive is the only steady grower: about 0.12 GB a day, and nothing prunes it.
- The live database bloated to 2.7 GB for about 17 MB of data before it was compacted by hand.
- Both were found by a person with `du` and psql.
The page shows none of it. `/api/fleet`'s health gives only the free space of the workspace root and TMPDIR, and Home's host section says the same.

Required behaviour.
(a) `/api/fleet`'s `health.storage`, read at the request as `disk` is:
- `free_bytes`: the free space of the workspace root's file system;
- `archive` {path, bytes, files, week_bytes}: the regular files under `<root>/.transcripts`, their apparent sizes summed, and the sizes of those whose last change is under 7 days old;
- `workspaces` {path, bytes}: the regular files under the root outside `.transcripts` and `.transcripts-progress`;
- `database` {bytes, tables}: `pg_database_size` of the store's database, and its five largest tables by `pg_total_relation_size`, as [{name, bytes}], largest first;
- `growth_bytes_per_day`: the archive's `week_bytes` over 7;
- `days_left`: `free_bytes` over `growth_bytes_per_day`, rounded down; null when the archive did not grow.
A part that cannot be read is null, and the rest still answers.
(b) web/src/resources.ts: `storageView(storage)` gives the card's words:
- `rows` [{name, size, note}]: "Transcript archive" with note "grows about <size> a day"; "Workspaces"; "Database" with note "largest: <table> <size>";
- `lasts`: "about <days> days at the archive's growth", the days grouped en-US; null when `days_left` is null.
A size reads "<n> MB" to one decimal under 1024 MB (1 MB is 1024 * 1024 bytes), and "<n> GB" to one decimal above.
(c) Home's host section shows a Storage card with those rows and that line.
(d) docs/storage.md names the figures.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/065.sh. `spawn serve` answers on a scratch database with a scratch workspace root:
- archive: `agent_a/a1.jsonl` (3 MiB, changed 1 day ago), `agent_a/a2.jsonl` (4 MiB, 3 days ago) and `agent_b/b1.jsonl` (5 MiB, 10 days ago). That is 12 MiB, 7 MiB of it in the last week, so 1 MiB a day.
- workspaces: `agent_c/big.bin`, 2 MiB.
Checks:
- (1) Through `GET /api/fleet`:
  - the archive is {bytes 12 MiB, files 3, week_bytes 7 MiB} and the workspaces 2 MiB;
  - growth is 1 MiB a day, and `days_left` is the answer's `free_bytes` over 1 MiB;
  - `free_bytes` and `database.bytes` agree with `df` and `pg_database_size`, read at once, within 1%, or 64 MiB of free space;
  - the five tables match psql's own list.
- (2) Under node, `storageView` over that answer gives:
  - the three rows, the archive "12.0 MB" with "grows about 1.0 MB a day";
  - the workspaces "2.0 MB", and the database's largest table named;
  - `lasts` from `days_left`, null without growth, and "3.0 GB" for 3 GiB.
It fails with 1 on 101077e2: there is no `health.storage`, and `storageView` does not exist.

The product reason. A disk that fills stops the fleet, and growth nobody can see is found only when something breaks. The owner has chosen to keep every transcript, so how fast the archive grows, and how long the disk lasts at that rate, is the figure that says when storage needs a decision. The database's size and largest tables beside it would have shown the 2.7 GB bloat on the page, weeks before anyone looked.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: unit tests of the walk (the archive and the progress directory left out of the workspaces, a file changed 8 days ago outside the week, an unreadable directory skipped), a spawn-postgres test of the database figures through the real store, and web/test tests for (b) and (c).
